action_summary: Round 3 discovered 76 doors and named its own next wall: nothing connected a GOAL to a door. This round joins them by measurement, and it took three designs because the first two were measured and found wrong. (1) Per-content conditions scored precision 0.4677 leave-one-out and 0.0 on the held-out tool: 33 gzip requests produced 33 different contents, so a join over identities had nothing to transfer. (2) The project's own five relations collapsed the surface into three move classes: they are all COMMUTATIVE, functions of a SET of pairs, so `mv a b` and `rm a` read identically. (3) The five relations plus LOT -- a function of the STEP, not of a state: can every readable content still be recovered afterwards -- separate retention from destruction without adding an observable, because the order of the two states was already recorded and `effect()` threw it away. Measured: 18 of 18 doors report an identical signature across three unrelated worlds (different filenames, different contents, different sizes), 60 of 60 held-out requests are answered from OTHER programs' rows, and 61 of 62 leave-one-out. The control that keeps that honest is reported alongside: `mv`'s move was matched by 59 of 59 candidates, so its answer carries no information, while `rm`'s was matched by 3 of 47. The saved row is (tool, relation signature, artifact span): no path, no argv, no content, no example -- which is the user's own objection answered, since exact experiences are never needed again but a relation shape is.

falsification_condition: The claim is false if a tool whose declaration is well-formed yields doors the tree does not confirm, or if a NO_EFFECT operation turns out to be a door under any constructible room, or if any trial leaves the tree altered. Each of those is a reported defect, not a tolerated one -- six such defects are recorded in the receipt.
honest_limits: This is not competence. Knowing 76 doors is not knowing which one a request wants; the census answers 'what can be done here', not 'what should be done'.
960 operations are UNCHARACTERISED, not dead. The census supplies what a usage line declares; a room with two files, a genuine patch, or a committed change is a stated decision it does not yet make.
git commit --all is knowingly mis-bound: git says 'paths with -a does not make sense' only in its ERROR, not its description, so the binder cannot read it without inventing a word list.
A room is a decision. git is judged inside a repository the census builds; changing which rooms exist changes the door count, so the room is stated per tool rather than hidden.
A GUI has no --help; that tier needs the accessibility tree or the DOM, and this sandbox has no display. man is also absent, so --help is the only declaration tier measured.
Producer-run sandbox only; no independent identity re-ran any of it; truth.achieved stays false.

load_bearing_primary.interpretation: OSWorld 2.0's authors diagnose frontier failure as weak recovery and maintenance of hidden state. A join that reads a goal as a demanded move of named relations, and knows which measured door produces that move, is the mechanism for choosing an action from state rather than guessing one. No benchmark task was run; no discharge is claimed.

next_step: The join answers WHICH door for a goal, not WHICH SEQUENCE for a goal that needs several moves. The pieces exist and are unjoined: perfect_algorithm_v1.plan() searches the learned model for a shortest path, and the census's environment can now carry a signature per transition, so a goal stated as a conjunction of moves is the next wall.
